subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The Last Mile: Power to Your Home
description: One-minute skill: The Last Mile: Power to Your Home.

hook.text: By the time electricity reaches your street, it's been stepped down three or four times.

buildup.text: Distribution lines run at 4 to 35 kV. A pole transformer drops that to 120 or 240V.

discovery.text: The transformer on your street serves maybe ten houses. It hums quietly around the clock.

twist.text: Underground cables cost five times more but resist storms. Cities prefer them.

climax.text: The last mile causes more outages than all transmission lines combined.

punchline.text: The weakest link in the grid is the wire to your door.

quiz.question: Why does the 'last mile' cause the most power outages?
options: Distribution lines are the oldest part of the grid
They are exposed to trees, storms, and accidents more than transmission lines
They carry the highest voltage in the system
